Chamarajanagara, Sitting At Kollegala, And Seeking
Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act'
for short) has been filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation,
against the judgment dated 04.03.2016 in MVC No.197/2010 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as 'the MACT' for short).
2. The injured claimant filed the claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.8,15,000/-.
The Tribunal NC: 2025:KHC:30844 HC-KAR considering the evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.2,48,880/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the claimant preferred this appeal.

3. It is contended that the compensation awarded under the heads pain and suffering, loss of amenities, loss of earning during laid up period are lower on side, and further the tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the claimant.
The claimant had sustained injures and suffering from disability to his right lower limb to an extent of 35%.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the trial court records.
5.
Injured
is aged about 28 years and is an agriculturist and a mason and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the income at Rs.6,000/- per month and it needs no interference.
As per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, the injured has sustained fracture of right tibia bone and doctor, who is examined as CW-1 assessed the disability as 35% to right lower limb.

sentences.text: He was hospitalized for a period of 34 days for more than one month.
Therefore, this Court finds it just and reasonable to enhance the compensation from Rs.20,000/- to 40,000/- under the head pain and suffering.
The appellant counsel submits that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head attendant charges, and the same is awarded Rs.15,000/- towards attendant charges.
6. It is contended that claimant underwent two surgeries and even after he discharged from the hospital, he took treatment and requested for loss of earning during laid up period for 5 months.
Considering the period of hospitalization, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation under the head loss of income during laid- up period of three months and it needs no interference.

7. Therefore, the appellant is entitled to enhanced compensation under the following heads:
NC: 2025:KHC:30844 HC-KAR Awarded by this Awarded by MACT High Court Rs.
Rs.
Medical Expenses 36,000/- 36,000/- Loss of income during laid up 18,000/-
18,000/- period Pain and suffering 20,000/- 40,000/- Loss of future 1,46,880/-
1,46,880/- earning capacity Nourishment, & 10,000/- 10,000/-
and diet Conveyance 8,000/- 8,000/-

Attendant charges NIL 15,000/-
Loss of amenities 10,000/- 10,000/-
In summary, the appellant/claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,83,880/- as opposed to Rs.2,48,880/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation amounts to Rs.35,000/-.
To this extent, the award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

9. The respondent, the Insurance Company, is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the certified copy NC: 2025:KHC:30844 HC-KAR of this order.
The entire enhanced compensation amount is to be released in favor of the appellant/claimant.
10. As per order dated 03.03.2025, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 862 days in filing the appeal.
11. The appeal is allowed in part.
